- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often overpredicts downward moves; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the 10–15 day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for spikes.
- Model overestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model lags; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
- Model frequently overshoots after strong sentiment-driven spikes; cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% above recent peak if sentiment remains positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is consistently positive over last 5 days, reduce forecast mean by 0.5–1.0% to account for overconfidence bias.
